quarterly_data.quarter: LS Eco Energy press release: release board (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: LS Eco Energy is investing KRW 11.6 billion to build a samarium metal production facility of about 240 tons a year at its LSCV site in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and plans trial mass production in December; the company says the volume is enough for about 700-1,000 tons a year of SmCo (samarium-cobalt) permanent magnets, used mainly in fighter jets and missiles, and calls it the first defense rare-earth metal production base outside China (company claim). It cites the US extending Defense Department supply-chain rules for SmCo magnets to the raw-material stage from January 2027. The release describes the structure as the first commercialisation of the Lynas cooperation: Lynas Rare Earths supplies the rare-earth feedstock, LS Eco Energy produces the metal in Vietnam and supplies it to LS Cable & System's permanent-magnet plant. The company plans to extend rare-earth metal production to dysprosium (Dy), terbium (Tb) and NdPr.
quarterly_data.figure: KRW 11.6 billion investment; about 240 tons a year samarium metal; trial mass production in December
